items.text: `Scheduler.get_jobs_for(func)` returns all jobs scheduled via `.do(func, ...)` regardless of arguments, or an empty list if none match. It matches by equality, not identity, so bound methods work. Its purpose is to let users query the Scheduler for jobs associated with a given function and cancel jobs without holding Job objects. Tests `test_get_jobs_for` and `test_get_jobs_for_bound_method` in test_schedule.py call it via `schedule.default_scheduler`; docs pick it up through the existing `autoclass:: schedule.Scheduler` entry. Committed on branch `feature/jobs-by-func` as 2c77dc4 (2026-11-03), not pushed.

items.text: Job tagging was added by Zerrossetto in Oct–Nov 2016 (ee730e5) to clear a subset of jobs easily, with tag type enforcement, set-based deduplication of repeated tags, generator expressions, and handling of a wrapped job cancelling its own scheduling; released in 0.4.0 (cca1e6f).

Job-query and execution features were added between 2020 and 2022: retrieving jobs per tag (#419), getting next run by tag (#463), execute-until functionality (#195), and a 'repeat' decorator (#148). Fixes included hour.at('MM:SS') parsing (#290), tuesday.at('HH:MM:SS') not running today (#331/#337), and long-running jobs no longer skipping periods.
`next_run()` throws ValueError when the job queue is empty (fixed July 30, 2013, issue #13, contributed by @mrhwick).

items.text: The at() method was extended in January 2019 by Nathan Wailes: it accepts timestamps with 1 second precision (fa151ef), supports recurring tasks like every().minute.at(':30') (6d248a4), the at(':SS') syntax bug was fixed (245728b), and the two-colon every().minute.at('::SS') syntax was removed with READMEs updated (c8f2e02). Its input validation was also tightened: it raises an exception if not passed a string in the right format (85a86f2), checks the format based on the selected units (846df18), and disallows whitespace (3b2ef20); docstrings were improved and redundant tests removed.

`at_time` support in schedule was extended in 2013: minutes can be set when the unit is hours, jobs with `at_time` run in the current hour if applicable, and `at_time` jobs run on the first day. Extra tests cover calling on the hour.

items.text: The schedule library supports job cancellation: users can control when a job stops running. Initially added in Aug 2013, then refined so that jobs return `CancelJob` instead of `False` and `remove` was renamed; followed by unit tests, a cancel_job bug fix, coverage restoration, and use of the Scheduler class's cancel_job.

Timezone handling is a major recent initiative in schedule: timezone support for .at() (#517, April 2022), fix for being off when using .at with timezone (#583), more timezone tests (#602), improved handling in next_run (#604), and timezone bugfixes (#623, May 2024). pytz is documented as a dependency when working with timezones (#601).

In January 2019 Nathan Wailes extended the schedule library's at() method: at() accepts timestamps with 1 second precision (fa151ef), supports recurring tasks like every().minute.at(':30') (6d248a4), fixed the at(':SS') syntax bug (245728b), and the two-colon every().minute.at('::SS') syntax was removed with READMEs updated (c8f2e02). | When: 2019-01-01 to 2019-01-08 | Involving: Nathan Wailes | Enable sub-minute scheduling with at()
